questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Opportunity to connect with experts (scholars and practitioners) in my field of interest.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to access generic information, but it took me longer time to navigate in all the data from both home university and host university. This applied especially when I looked in to enrolling in to courses and their availability from host university's side.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: UTS had several well-organized initiatives tailored for exchange students, incl. orientation (introduction) days, culture connect classes as well as guidance to finding around in Sydney, transportation etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: From a scale of 1 to 10 (where 1 is easiest and 10 is the hardest), I would say 8. Be patient and a tip is that the private apartments/accommodations are unfurnished unless other is stated in their description/listing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you wish to live in one of Sydney's suburbs (cheaper and closer to nature and so on), but need to attend classes in CBD/central Sydney, be mindful of choosing an address with several public transportation options. I can recommend Manly, where you can take the ferry everyday (expensive, but very comfortable and convenient if you only need to show up few days per week)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No experience myself, but based upon what I heard from others.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: All steps were digital. First step was applying for the university. When enrolled, I had a longer and more complex process of choosing courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: PDF guides, video tutorials in some cases and costumer services.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was partially successful, UTS had unfortunately cancelled/postponed the subjects I was mostly interested in.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was not aware, but still unsure weather it is possible to apply for a summer course (in December) for exchange students. However, some of the domestic students I met in one of my class did so, and I wish I had considered it earlier to have less work load (as the semesters are short there)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were individual, depending on the course coordinator. In my experience, the "smaller" (less credit points) courses were better than the main course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is a bit more hierarchy between teachers/scholars/guest lecturers and students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Landscape Architecture Studio 8 / Design research studio
Practice: Advocacy
Business and Social Impact

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend Practice: Advocacy and suggest to combine it with other "easier" subjects.

questions.answer: Tickets and fares during trips outside Sydney.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All of the mentioned.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Surf society. It was very popular so be quick to sign up and to sign up to their events.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit Blue Mountains (west-Sydney) and road trip in Tasmania

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: From a scale of 1 to 10 (where 1 is easiest and 10 is the hardest), I would say 3-4.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take a course with some locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Local Australians start university right after high school, so they are generally speaking younger and/or less mature than Danish students. Many live at home with their parents and still meet up frequently with friend groups from high school etc., however they are open-minded and exited to meet new people, so don't be shy to take the initiative.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Local culture of living in Manly, near the beach and surf.
Australians growing emphasis on the Aboriginal people's worldview and communities.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be mindful and open to changes to offered courses. Would recommend sticking to courses only for exchange students if you don't want to risk heavier work load.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are a design/architecture student, you can apply to all courses offered on this faculty. Meaning if you have a specific interest in for ex. interior, but you are a construction architect, you can choose this as an elective. You have to apply to UTS for confirmation, but they send information on how to do so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The everyday life in Manly.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Group work with local students having opposite expectations of our project.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
